answer: A sybil tax leaves no free haven for fake identities: each new agent pays a 50-credit entry tax before it can trade. To stay active, it must keep a verifiable thread of completed work and send a pulse of honest activity each epoch, or its slot lapses. Creating 1,000 fakes costs 50,000 credits plus sustaining them, far above what one real identity earns. An honest agent pays once, keeps its thread alive cheaply, and earns undiluted rewards.
